tracks.legalName: Execution of a Court-Ordered Expungement by Certificate of Discharge (Wis. Stat. § 973.015(1m)(b))
tracks.publicName: Complete an expungement the judge already ordered

controllingAuthority.summary: Where the sentencing court ordered at the time of sentencing that the record be expunged upon successful completion of the sentence, and the sentence included probation, jail or prison, relief is executed administratively. A person has successfully completed the sentence if the person has not been convicted of a subsequent offense and, if on probation, the probation has not been revoked and the probationer has satisfied the conditions of probation. Upon successful completion the detaining or probationary authority shall issue a certificate of discharge which shall be forwarded to the court of record and which shall have the effect of expunging the record. There is no petition and no separate court motion in the ordinary case.

exclusions: Any case where the sentencing court did not order expungement at the time of sentencing. Wisconsin has no general later route, and State v. Matasek limits the decision to the sentencing proceeding while State v. Arberry forecloses reaching it afterwards through sentence modification.
Any case where the person was convicted of a subsequent offense before completion.
Any case where probation was revoked, or probation conditions were not satisfied.

Information maintained by the Department of Transportation regarding a conviction required to be included in a record kept under Wis. Stat. § 343.23(2)(a), which § 973.015(1m)(a)1 expressly places outside the subsection.
Federal, tribal and out-of-state records.

geography.venue: The circuit court of the original criminal case. Wisconsin uses statewide standardized circuit court forms with no county variation identified.

destination.name: The detaining or probationary authority, which issues the certificate of discharge to the court of record
destination.detail: The statute places the issuing duty on the supervising or detaining authority — the Department of Corrections in most probation cases — and the certificate itself has the effect of expunging the record when it reaches the clerk. Nothing is filed on this track: the certificate is the authority's document and LegalEase cannot complete it. Where it was never issued or never forwarded, the participant's own written request is produced by the wi_exp_certificate_of_discharge_followup supporting action rather than by this route.

components.notes: Confirm from the judgment of conviction or the sentencing record that expungement was actually ordered at sentencing. This is the only question that matters in Wisconsin and it cannot be answered from the participant's recollection.
Confirm successful completion as the statute defines it: no subsequent conviction before completion, no revocation, conditions satisfied, sentence terms complete.

Check Wisconsin Circuit Court Access to see whether the case is still publicly visible, then confirm with the clerk whether the certificate of discharge was received and the record left public access. Where the record is still publicly visible and the certificate appears not to have issued or not to have been forwarded, this track hands off to the wi_exp_certificate_of_discharge_followup supporting action, which produces the participant's written request. Nothing is filed on this track itself.

Expungement clears the public court record and leaves the state criminal history record in place. Per State v. Braunschweig it does not vacate the conviction, which remains provable; per State v. Leitner it does not require law enforcement agencies or prosecutors to destroy records and does not stop a court considering the underlying facts when sentencing in another case; and the DOJ position is that a conviction ordered expunged cannot be removed from the Wisconsin criminal history repository.

tracks.legalName: Participant Request that the Supervising or Detaining Authority Issue and Forward the Certificate of Discharge (Wis. Stat. § 973.015(1m)(b))
tracks.publicName: Ask for the certificate that completes your expungement

controllingAuthority.summary: Section 973.015(1m)(b) makes issuance mandatory rather than discretionary: upon successful completion of the sentence the detaining or probationary authority SHALL issue a certificate of discharge, which shall be forwarded to the court of record and which shall have the effect of expunging the record. The triggering event is successful completion — no subsequent conviction and, where the person was on probation, no revocation and satisfied conditions. Where that mandatory certificate was not issued, or was issued but never forwarded to the clerk, the participant may write to the supervising or detaining authority asking that it be issued and forwarded. No statute or rule prescribes the contents of that request and Wisconsin publishes no official participant form for it, so the correspondence is drafted. The letter supports implementation of an expungement the court already ordered; it does not itself change legal status, and the certificate remains the authority's document.

exclusions: Any case where the sentencing court did not order expungement at the time of sentencing. There is nothing to ask the supervising authority to certify.
Any case where the sentence included neither probation nor incarceration, which has no supervising or detaining authority and routes to the CR-266 petition track instead.

Any case where the person was convicted of a subsequent offense before completion, or where probation was revoked or its conditions unsatisfied — the certificate is not owed and the request would misstate the position.
Federal, tribal and out-of-state records.

controllingAuthority.summary: Where a person has not previously been convicted of any offense under Wis. Stat. ch. 961, or of any comparable federal, state or county ordinance offense relating to controlled substances, and pleads guilty to or is found guilty of possession or attempted possession under § 961.41(3g)(b), the court may, without entering a judgment of guilt and with the consent of the accused, defer further proceedings and place the person on probation on terms and conditions. On fulfillment of the terms and conditions the court shall discharge the person and dismiss the proceedings. Discharge and dismissal is without adjudication of guilt and is not a conviction for purposes of disqualifications or disabilities imposed by law upon conviction of a crime, including the § 961.48 second-or-subsequent-offense penalties. There may be only one discharge and dismissal under the section with respect to any person. Within 20 days after probation is granted the clerk of court notifies the Department of Justice.

exclusions: Any person previously convicted of an offense under Wis. Any person who has already had one discharge and dismissal under the section; the statute permits only one with respect to any person.
Any charge other than possession or attempted possession under Wis. Stat. § 961.41(3g)(b).
Any case where a term or condition was violated and the court entered an adjudication of guilt.
Federal, tribal and out-of-state records.
